references.text: Moses' instructions about cities of refuge where someone who kills another by accident can flee and be safe from the avenger of blood until they stand trial before the assembly.
Detailed laws concerning unintentional killing without enmity or premeditation, allowing the killer to seek refuge in a city of refuge.
Parallel legislation regarding cities of refuge, specifically addressing one who kills their neighbor unknowingly and without prior hatred.
The fulfillment of the commandment about cities of refuge during Joshua's time, with the same purpose: to protect someone who kills by accident.
The list of designated cities of refuge where anyone who kills another by accident can flee.
The fundamental law concerning a place of refuge for one who did not plan the killing but whom God allowed to happen through their hand.
A New Testament reference to fleeing in order to seize the hope set before us, a spiritual parallel to the city of refuge.
